newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn, soy and wheat steady.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn, soy and wheat steady.

text.p: U.S. FOB Gulf corn, soybean and wheat offers were steady amid quiet activity ahead of the Easter holiday weekend, export sources said.
Dealers cited ample supplies at the Gulf and lackluster demand despite encouraging weekly export sales and barge traffic problems near the mouth of the Mississippi River.

The Mississippi River crested at Vicksburg, Miss., on Thursday as floodwaters from snow melting in the Midwest and spring rains flowed downriver, emergency officials said. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers opened 298 of 350 flood bays on the Bonnet Carre Spillway above New Orleans to prevent flooding.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported higher than expected wheat export sales of 497,000 tonnes, well above trade expectations for 100,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
USDA put weekly soybean export sales at 387,000 tonnes and soymeal sales at a larger than expected 209,800 tonnes.
It also reported net weekly corn sales of 569,500 tonnes, compared with trade estimates of 400,000 to 700,000.
